confirmed: The local source is the 19-page journal article by Eduardo Silva-Fuentealba, European Public & Social Innovation Review 9, 1-19, DOI 10.31637/epsir-2024-410; received 27/05/2024, accepted 10/07/2024 and published 12/08/2024. The full markdown and all PDF pages were read, including references and end matter (p. 1; pp. 17-19).

One study used the same school population before and after the intervention, explicitly without a control group; no random assignment of people or condition order is described. design_class = quasi_people, context_class = observational, core = no and has_randomized_people_study = false are supported (p. 6, Sections 2-2.1).

Participants were seventh-grade students aged 12-13 at one science-humanities school in the O'Higgins region of Chile; the results describe three courses A, B and C. These are people observed at two timepoints, not two independent participant samples (p. 6, Section 2; p. 15, Section 3.5).

Students used ChatGPT to generate ideas, develop song lyrics and structure text and harmonic progression, with instruction on interacting with it. The scored task was TTCT verbal form A before and after that activity; elaboration was excluded (p. 4, Section 1.2; pp. 6-7, Sections 2-2.1).

The paper describes ChatGPT as based on GPT-3 in its background section, as the form qualifies; it does not separately document the model version used during the intervention (p. 5, Section 1.3; pp. 6-7, Section 2.1).

Originality: pretest mean 12,54, 95% CI 11,39-13,70, median 12,00; posttest mean 14,21, 95% CI 12,96-15,47, median 13,50. Paired Wilcoxon Sig. 0,000, with the null rejected. The reported string matches; no dimension-specific SD is printed (p. 10, Gráfico 2, embedded table inspected; p. 13, Tabla 3).

Flexibility: pretest mean 3,19, 95% CI 2,50-3,87, median 3,00; posttest mean 4,31, 95% CI 3,51-5,12, median 4,00. Paired Wilcoxon Sig. 0,000, with the null rejected. The reported string matches; no dimension-specific SD is printed (p. 10, Gráfico 2, embedded table inspected; p. 13, Tabla 3).

Fluency: pretest mean 7,84, 95% CI 7,13-8,55, median 7,00; posttest mean 7,77, 95% CI 6,75-8,79, median 7,00. Paired Wilcoxon Sig. 0,517, with the null retained. The reported string matches; no dimension-specific SD is printed (p. 10, Gráfico 2, embedded table inspected; p. 13, Tabla 3).

The one-line finding's final-score means and SDs, 23,57 (8,485) before and 26,30 (11,395) after, match Tabla 2. Tabla 3 additionally reports Sig. 0,000 for Final E versus Final S; its footnote identifies the significance values as asymptotic (p. 8, Tabla 2; p. 13, Tabla 3).

The posttest is described as following the creative activity, but the source does not explicitly state AI availability during the scored TTCT or the time lag. The after_ai coding follows that procedural sequence and should not be presented as direct confirmation of AI removal or a delayed assessment (p. 6, Section 2.1).

This is an original empirical article, not a synthesis; no pooled estimates or study/effect-size counts apply. No supplement, appendix, data repository or code repository is identified in the article (p. 1, article type; pp. 6-16, methods/results/discussion; pp. 17-19, end matter).
The author reports no external funding and no conflict of interest; no company role in conducting the study is reported (p. 19, funding and conflict-of-interest statements).
summary: The paper reports one uncontrolled pretest-posttest study, so its quasi_people/observational classification and exclusion from the randomized core are correct. The reported statistics match the PDF, but the participant count is inferred from normality-test gl, the overall TTCT outcome is omitted, and several descriptions or structured fields need correction.
